### What does this PR do?

`global_profiler.global_tool_config.torch.contents` and `.discrete` were silently ignored. The actor, critic, and ref role configs hardcoded `tool_config.torch.contents: []` and `discrete: false`, instead of interpolating from the global config the way `nsys.discrete` (`actor.yaml` line 221) and every `torch_memory` field already do. Rollout mirrors the actor config, so it inherited the same gap.

The empty contents fall back to `[CPU, CUDA]` activities inside `torch_profile.py` (`verl/utils/profiler/torch_profile.py:200-212`), so listing `cpu`/`cuda` globally appeared to work by coincidence, while `stack` (the `with_stack` flag, `torch_profile.py:231`) was dropped outright — a global setting of `contents=["cpu","cuda","stack"]` produced traces with no call stacks.

This wires the two fields through `${oc.select:global_profiler.global_tool_config.torch.*,default}` in the actor/critic/ref yamls, regenerates the `_generated_*.yaml` reference files, adds a CPU test, and documents the global path.

Found while profiling a training run with `++global_profiler.global_tool_config.torch.contents=["cpu","cuda","stack"]`: the collected trace had kernel/cpu_op activity but no stacks, and stream-level event attribution was impossible.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Searched open PRs and issues for [profiler](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+profiler), [torch profiler](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22torch+profiler%22), [global_tool_config](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+global_tool_config), and open [profiler issues](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+profiler). The closest open PRs are #8290 (nsight capture counting) and #4707 (torch profiler save/validation logic in `profile.py`); neither touches this config wiring, and no open issue reports it.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`: `[perf, trainer] fix: forward global torch profiler contents/discrete to role tool configs`.

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/test_profiler_torch_tool_config_on_cpu.py   # 8 passed
python -m pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_config_on_cpu.py \
    tests/workers/config/test_actor_config_on_cpu.py \
    tests/workers/config/test_critic_config_on_cpu.py                             # 14 passed, 10 skipped (missing optional deps locally)
bash scripts/generate_trainer_config.sh                                           # regenerated files match the committed ones
pre-commit run --files <all changed files>                                        # all hooks passed
```

The new test was verified to fail on the pre-fix yamls (4 inheritance failures) and pass after the fix. A manual compose of `ppo_trainer` with the launcher override below confirms all four roles resolve `contents` to `["cpu","cuda","stack"]`.

### API and Usage Example

No API change; a previously-ignored config path now takes effect.

```bash
# before: contents=["cpu","cuda","stack"] stopped at the global layer; workers saw []
# after: all roles (actor, critic, ref, rollout) honor it
--config global_profiler.tool=torch \
    ++global_profiler.global_tool_config.torch.contents='["cpu","cuda","stack"]'
```

Role-level overrides (`actor_rollout_ref.actor.profiler.tool_config.torch.contents=...`) still take precedence, as before.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/trainer/config/actor/actor.yaml`, `critic/critic.yaml`, `ref/ref.yaml`: `tool_config.torch.contents` and `.discrete` become `${oc.select:global_profiler.global_tool_config.torch.contents,[]}` / `${oc.select:global_profiler.global_tool_config.torch.discrete,false}`, matching the existing `nsys.discrete` and `torch_memory` patterns in the same files. Rollout already interpolates from the actor config, so no change there.
- The four `verl/trainer/config/_generated_*.yaml` files regenerated via `scripts/generate_trainer_config.sh`.
- `tests/trainer/ppo/test_profiler_torch_tool_config_on_cpu.py`: composes the full `ppo_trainer` config and asserts the global torch settings reach actor/ref/rollout/critic, and that defaults stay `[]`/`false` when the global block is unset.
- `docs/perf/torch_profiling.md`: documents the global `contents`/`discrete` path.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — all hooks passed (including the `_generated_*.yaml` sync check).
- [x] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs): `docs/perf/torch_profiling.md`.
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s): `tests/trainer/ppo/test_profiler_torch_tool_config_on_cpu.py`, a CPU-only Hydra compose test following the existing `_on_cpu.py` convention; no GPU test needed since this is pure config wiring.
- [ ] Once ready for CI, send a message in the [ci-request channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) — will be done by the human submitter.
- [ ] Not applicable: this PR does not change the `recipe` submodule.

+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest

+    with initialize_config_dir(version_base=None, config_dir=str(CONFIG_DIR)):

+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("torch_path", ROLE_TORCH_PATHS)
+def test_global_torch_settings_reach_role_config(torch_path):
+    overrides = [

+        "++global_profiler.global_tool_config.torch.discrete=true",
+    ]
+    cfg = _compose_ppo_trainer(overrides)
+    torch_cfg = OmegaConf.select(cfg, torch_path)
+    assert list(torch_cfg.contents) == ["cpu", "cuda", "stack"]
+    assert torch_cfg.discrete is True
+

+    torch_cfg = OmegaConf.select(cfg, torch_path)
+    assert list(torch_cfg.contents) == []

 * **`profile_token_end`**: Effective only for the rollout role; defines the stop response-token index (exclusive) for rollout decoding collection. It is applied only when valid (0-based, `profile_token_end > profile_token_start`, and within response length).
 * **`schedule`**: Optional [`torch.profiler.schedule`](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/profiler.html#torch.profiler.schedule) over the **update loop's mini-batches**, so an update stage with many identical mini-batches does not bloat its trace. `verl` advances it once per update mini-batch; the log-prob forwards and rollout are never sub-sampled. Enabled only when `active > 0`. The full `skip_first`/`wait`/`warmup`/`active`/`repeat` selects which update mini-batches are captured in both modes. In **continuous mode** (`discrete: False`) skipping ahead to a later mini-batch also drops the earlier stages (rollout, log-prob) from that one shared trace; leave `skip_first`/`wait`/`warmup` at 0 to keep them. In **`discrete: True` mode** the update stage is isolated in its own trace, so the other stages keep their own full traces regardless. It never emits torch's `ProfilerStep#<n>` rows. See [Scheduling the update loop's mini-batches](#3-scheduling-the-update-loops-mini-batches).
